insights.observation: Food delivery plus eating out (Swiggy, Zomato, Domino's, Third Wave) adds up to roughly ₹4,680 across 8 orders — almost matching your whole month of groceries at ₹8,847.
insights.whyItMatters: As a student, delivery feels like a small convenience each time, but the monthly total is where it quietly competes with the savings habit you said you want. For a family earner, the same number would read as shared meals rather than solo orders — context changes the story.
insights.action: This week, swap 2 delivery orders for a home-cooked meal or a mess plan and move the ~₹700 saved into your SIP the same day.

insights.observation: Your one Delhi trip cost ₹7,398 (IndiGo ₹5,499 + OYO ₹1,899) — the single biggest event in the month, bigger than rent-adjacent bills combined.
insights.whyItMatters: One-off trips like this are exactly what irregular income needs a buffer for: the money is well spent, but without a travel sinking fund it lands entirely on one month. A professional with regular salary absorbs it; a freelancer feels it twice.
insights.action: Start a ₹1,000/month auto-transfer labelled 'next trip' — 15 minutes in your banking app, then forget it.

insights.observation: Three quiet subscriptions — Netflix ₹649, Spotify ₹119, YouTube Premium ₹139 — total ~₹907/month, or ~₹10,884 a year, charged whether you watch or not.
insights.whyItMatters: Subscriptions are the opposite of your weekend movie night (PVR ₹890, concert ₹1,999): those you chose and remember, these renew silently. With entertainment as a priority, keeping the one you love and pausing the rest protects the fun while trimming the leak.
insights.action: Check screen-time for each app this week and pause the least-used one — most cancellations take under 5 minutes.
